transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~50m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (CTO, Summit AI), Ava Thompson (ML Engineer), Liam Patel (Head of Infra)

Summary: quick walkthrough of Redwood Optimize quant profiles, demo of INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs, show quality vs latency numbers, discuss next steps for benchmarks and security docs.

00:00 Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you taking the time, um quick round of intros?
00:06 Carlos Mendes: yeah hey i'm carlos, cto at summit, we run real-time chat summarization and retrieval augmented generation, latency is super important for our product.
00:12 Ava Thompson: ava here - ml engineer, i'm focused on quality regressions and prompt robustness, we've seen quality drops with some quant profiles in the past.
00:20 Jordan Lee: totally, that is exactly what we're covering today, priya will lead the deep dive on INT8/FP8 profiles and we'll show quality vs latency numbers and a few knobs in Redwood Optimize.
00:28 Priya Nair: great hi all, i'll share my screen in a sec, first, quick context — Redwood Optimize recommends quant profiles based on workload shape, sequence length distribution, and quality SLOs. we typically evaluate INT8 and FP8 variants.
00:42 Liam Patel: quick question, do you mean FP8 like the nvidia-s style fp8 or a custom emulation?
00:47 Priya Nair: good call, it's the nvidia-style FP8 path that our runtime supports; we also have an emulation path for other hw that approximates fp8 behaviour. there's some noise there but it's close.
00:58 Jordan Lee: one note — when we say INT8 here it's actually per-layer or mixed precision int8 in many cases, so it's not a single blunt instrument.
01:10 Priya Nair: right yeah, mixed per-layer int8 + fp32 residuals, we can tune per-block. okay pulling up the quality vs latency slides.
01:25 [screen share sound]
01:30 Priya Nair: here's a real example from a customer with conversational summarization — baseline fp16 latency 220ms p95, INT8 reduces token compute so p95 drops to around 140-150ms, FP8 gives ~120-130ms depending on kernel selection. quality measured by rouge/bleu-ish proxies and an internal human eval: INT8 had a small 1.8% quality delta, FP8 about 0.9% delta on our internal benchmark.
01:55 Carlos Mendes: okay those numbers look promising, but what about hallucinations? we can't accept regressions that lead to factual errors.
02:02 Priya Nair: totally, we track hallucination metrics in Optimize — we run a targeted prompt set, and if hallucination hits a threshold we flag profiles. for summit's workload we'd want to run your prompt set; small delta on generic benchmarks doesn't always capture domain-specific failure modes.
02:18 Ava Thompson: makes sense, so we should send you our golden prompts.
02:22 Jordan Lee: yes please, that will be part of the pilot.
02:25 Priya Nair: also note batching and KV cache behaviour changes latency — if you have long context and active KV cache hits, the effective latency can be lower than our synthetic token-only numbers. batching improves throughput but can hurt tail latency if misconfigured.
02:42 Liam Patel: can you expand on the KV cache comment? we currently shard KV across nodes and have some custom caching in front.
02:49 Priya Nair: sure — in Redwood runtime we aggressively reuse kv cache across warm sessions; however quantized kernels sometimes change memory layout so cache warm-up patterns differ, we add a small warm-up pass in Optimize to mitigate. sometimes transcripts show a small re-alloc pause which can spike p99 on cold starts.
03:10 Jordan Lee: and those spikes are usually mitigated with pre-warming or short-lived dedicated instances as part of a canary.
03:17 Carlos Mendes: what about dedicated vs hosted — we prefer to keep data in our VPC for now. does Redwood Optimize behave the same on Dedicated?
03:24 Priya Nair: yes the Optimize recommendations apply across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. kernel availability may differ by underlying gpu flavor but the optimizer maps to best available kernel. in Dedicated you get more predictable latency, and our autoscale + burst configs help with tail control.
03:40 Ava Thompson: perf vs cost — could you share cost delta numbers for INT8 vs FP8?
03:45 Priya Nair: rough thumb rule: INT8 usually gives 30-45% token compute reduction vs fp16, FP8 gives 40-55% depending on hw and sequence length. cost also depends on batching; we provide a cost model spreadsheet which i'll share.
03:58 Jordan Lee: noted — jordan: action item, i'll share the spreadsheet after the call.
04:05 [pause]
04:10 Priya Nair: quick demo — i ran a local perf run on a 4k context model with summit-like prompts, here's latency histogram. [shows chart] you can see that with optimized FP8 kernels p95 drops but p99 sometimes creeps up unless we tune burst config.
04:28 Ava Thompson: hmm that p99 is our worry, users notice those spikes. can you do more aggressive autoscale?
04:33 Priya Nair: you can, but there's a tradeoff vs cost. in Dedicated we can set short-lived spare capacity to absorb spikes — that's usually good for user-facing endpoints.
04:45 Carlos Mendes: security wise, we'll need SOC2 and SSO details. do you have audit logs for model invocations?
04:52 Jordan Lee: yep SOC2 docs and SSO/SAML guides, we also support KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments; audit logs are available at token- and route-level in Redwood Console. i'll send docs.
05:03 Liam Patel: any concerns about data residency? some of our EU customers require data to remain in EU.
05:08 Priya Nair: we can run in-region and Private deployments, yes — region pinning and GC retention policies are supported.
05:14 Ava Thompson: can you walk through a sample pilot timeline? how long to get meaningful quality results?
05:19 Priya Nair: typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: week 1 instrument and run baseline, week 2 run quantized profiles with golden prompts, week 3 human eval and tuning, week 4 if needed run dedicated perf tests. shorter if you have small sample set.
05:33 Carlos Mendes: ok that's reasonable. what's the impact on embeddings? we also do re-ranking and semantic search.
05:38 Priya Nair: embeddings are usually FP16 or int8 quantized differently; re-ranking quality can be sensitive so we typically recommend running an A/B on embedding drift; Optimize includes an embedding drift checker.
05:50 Jordan Lee: i'm going to pull up the proposed pilot deck and timeline.
06:00 [screen change]
06:05 Priya Nair: here's the baseline v quant graphs for rouge proxy and human score. note the variance bars — for some prompt families INT8 variance is higher, that's why we do per-prompt family profiles.
06:20 Ava Thompson: would we be able to programmatically pin certain routes to FP8 and others to INT8? some non-critical paths could use INT8 for cost savings.
06:29 Priya Nair: yes you can route by policy: route X -> INT8, route Y -> FP8; canary and A/B built-in. the runtime will pick compatible kernels or fallback to fp16 if needed.
06:40 Carlos Mendes: any gotchas with function calling or streaming? our product streams partial results back to clients.
06:45 Priya Nair: streaming is supported; quantization doesn't change the streaming protocol but it can change chunking behaviour slightly. function calling payloads are unaffected but larger tokenization patterns can shift latency profiles.
06:58 [brief laughter]
07:02 Jordan Lee: let's surface a concrete measurement plan — we'll need: your golden prompts, traffic profile, success criteria (latency p95/p99, quality cutoffs), and a decision threshold for switching profiles.
07:15 Ava Thompson: we'll draft those and send by monday.
07:18 Carlos Mendes: for the perf run can we use our internal infra or should we run on Redwood Dedicated?
07:24 Priya Nair: recommend both — run a short sanity on your infra and then larger reproducible with Redwood Dedicated so we can control kernels and load. we can help you with test harness.
07:36 Jordan Lee: i'll coordinate scheduling.
07:38 Priya Nair: quick demo of Optimize UI — you can see recommended profiles per-model, per-route, a slider to prioritize quality vs latency, and an evaluation tab with A/B results and hallucination flags.
07:52 Ava Thompson: nice, can those recommendations be exported as terraform or api configs?
07:56 Priya Nair: yes, config-as-code export and api endpoints so you can integrate with infra pipelines.
08:04 Liam Patel: what's the expected engineering work on our side for the pilot?
08:08 Jordan Lee: mostly provide prompts, traffic and a short integration step for the test harness, plus a contact for dev ops. Redwood will run the Optimize experiments.
08:18 Carlos Mendes: ok sounds manageable.
08:21 Priya Nair: last section — edge cases and known issues: FP8 on older drivers sometimes causes minor numeric drift; we recommend driver 535+ on nvidia for best fp8 kernels. also watch out for mixed-cpu/gpu inference paths — keep inference on supported gpu.
08:41 Ava Thompson: are there any licensing limitations? we use a few open models under community licenses.
08:45 Jordan Lee: we support open models and also charge per-token for hosted; Dedicated billing is different. legal can review model licenses if needed.
08:54 [crosstalk] 
08:58 Priya Nair: ok, recap of next steps: jordan will share spreadsheet and pricing, priya will run sims and provide recommended profile set, summit provides prompts/traffic, schedule pilot start next week if possible.
09:15 Carlos Mendes: that works. thanks for the clear walkthrough.
09:20 Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and timeline.
09:25 [meeting ends]

Notes on transcript quality: occasional speaker label mixups and small transcription errors (e.g., "K V cache" vs "KV cache", "fp8" sometimes capitalized FP8), natural filler words and overlaps preserved.
